findings.current: With every stride, it closed the three-meter gap in an instant.
findings.defect: The draft turns the three meters covered by each stride into a single three-meter gap, altering the golem’s movement and distance.
findings.rationale: The source states that each individual stride closes three meters of distance.
findings.replacement: With every stride, it ate up three meters in an instant.
findings.source: 보폭 한 번에 3m의 거리가 휙휙 좁혀진다.

findings.current: But he couldn’t blame them. Their bodies, already sensing the threat to their lives, had moved toward the front line of their own accord.
findings.defect: The draft invents Im Kkeokjeong’s judgment that he could not blame them. The source instead says the recruits had no choice because their endangered bodies moved on their own.
findings.rationale: The omitted subject follows the new Guild members, while 어쩔 수 없었다 expresses their lack of choice rather than Im Kkeokjeong’s sympathy.
findings.replacement: But they had no choice. Their bodies, already sensing the threat to their lives, moved toward the front line of their own accord.
findings.source: 그러나 어쩔 수 없었다. 이미 생명의 위협을 느낀 몸뚱어리가 저절로 일선을 향해 움직였다.

findings.current:
“I woke up every night. How could you have seen me?”

“Huh?”

“It was always the middle of the night when I opened my eyes. I was tired, so I just went back to sleep.”
findings.defect: The draft changes 새벽, the dawn or early-morning hours, into the middle of the night in both lines.
findings.rationale: Taekyung specifically claims that he woke around dawn, which supports his excuse that Hayeon would not have seen him.
findings.replacement:
“I woke up around dawn each day. How could you have seen me?”

“Huh?”

“Every time I opened my eyes, it was around dawn. I was tired, so I just kept sleeping.”
findings.source:
“새벽마다 깼는데 네가 어떻게 봐?”

“어?”

“눈뜰 때마다 새벽이더라. 피곤해서 그냥 쭉 잤어.”

findings.current: “What kind of workshop lasts a whole week? Are we going to Pyeongchang or Gapyeong?”
findings.defect: The untranslated place names lack the brief cultural context needed for the joke contrasting ordinary domestic retreat destinations with the grander possibilities that follow.
findings.rationale: A concise footnote preserves the implication that these are conventional nearby choices for a company or organization workshop.
findings.replacement:
“What kind of workshop lasts a whole week? Are we going to Pyeongchang or Gapyeong?[^1]”

[^1]: Pyeongchang and Gapyeong are popular domestic getaway destinations in South Korea, often used for group retreats.
findings.source: “아니, 무슨 워크숍을 일주일이나…… 평창이나 가평 쪽으로 가는 겁니까?”

findings.current: “Damn it, I should’ve been a damage dealer instead of a tank.”
findings.defect: “Damn it” softens the coarse expletive 염병 and weakens the speaker’s panicked, profane complaint.
findings.rationale: 염병 is a strong, vulgar interjection here, so the English should retain comparable force.
findings.replacement: “Fuck, I should’ve gone with damage dealer instead of tank.”

findings.current: Hayeon nodded solemnly. Mom, who had been listening quietly, spoke with an expression like her heart had just collapsed.
findings.defect: “Her heart had just collapsed” is an unnatural literal rendering of the Korean idiom 억장이 무너지다.
findings.rationale: The source describes the mother as emotionally devastated, not as though her physical heart had collapsed.
findings.replacement: Hayeon nodded solemnly. Mom, who had been listening quietly, looked utterly crushed as she spoke.
findings.source: 하연이가 숙연한 얼굴로 고개를 끄덕였고, 가만히 듣고 있던 엄마는 억장이 무너진 듯한 표정으로 말했다.

findings.defect: The draft drops the crude intensifying force of 개, making Taekyung’s punchline noticeably milder.
findings.rationale: 개꿀 is emphatic vulgar slang, and the stronger phrasing preserves Taekyung’s irreverent gamer voice.

summary: The draft contains one altered movement quantity, one altered narrative subject, a timing shift in Taekyung’s lie, an unexplained culturally specific location contrast, and several localized register or phrasing issues.
